posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
I do not have access to that, and I am unable to find the exact thing, however I do not see what this is necessary? You can take any project/group of files and use it to learn CLEs. Actually, I would recommend against trying to get the same set of files, to prevent rote-learning and encourage actually exploring the CLEs. The point of the video is to demonstrate what can be done with vim/emacs, and I would suggest using the video as a motivation, and then trying things out by yourself, on a set of files of your choosing. Do not blindly copy the same steps/commands demonstrated in the videos, it is a habit that leads you to not actually learn anything.

Github is full of open-source projects with source files, and you can use literally anything (maybe better if you also understand the code, but not required) to learn how to use CLEs to manipulate files. Heres one example I could find by searching online that looked similar, however you can use literally any text file under the sun. Or, as Ishan suggested, create your own.

posts.cooked: I actually meant to get that so as to just practice the set of commands taught in the course, like editing and trying new commands in vi with the .c files and all. Thanks for directing to the example, I actually forgot that github does have open source codes that I can use for this, now I would try them out. There was no intention of rote learning, it’s just that I needed a few files to experiment with the vi editor.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Sure, feel free to try out other files too, and more importantly, other set of commands of vi/emacs that are not demonstrated directly in the video, as it serves as only a motivation to get started. Refer to vim cheat sheets or vim adventure, as well as the vimtutor command.
